Texas State University's AI pavement inspection method

Carousel No. 22, September 12th, 2026

Shipped at 6.92

This run did not merge, so the images below come from the run branch claude/daily-2026-09-12 rather than from main. They stop resolving if that branch is deleted.

What degraded

  • THE DECK WAS SCORED THREE TIMES AND SHIPPED ON THE THIRD. Round 2's three judges all terminated on the same session rate limit inside a second of each other, so round 2 is a retry of one lens rather than a panel. That retry raised a HARD FAIL on frame 8, correctly, and the round 3 panel scored the repaired deck at a 6.92 median with no hard fail from any of the three.
  • FRAME 8 PRINTED TWO NUMERALS THAT TRACED TO NOTHING, and both numeral gates were green over them. It labelled its axis bounds 1.0 and 0. aggregate_check cannot declare a bare axis label, so the declaration was refused, and numeral_trace passed them because the digits 1 and 0 occur somewhere in the evidence of a claim the frame cites, which is the coincidence its own docstring names as the case it cannot see. The first disposition was to ship them undeclared with a paragraph of explanation. That was wrong and the judge said so twice. The frame now draws both rules and names them SCALE TOP and SCALE BASE, printing no bound figure.
  • TWO CI FAILURES ON THIS PR WERE RED ON main TOO AND ARE FIXED HERE. The Lone Star mark landed on the front page headline at every desktop width from 768 to 1440, because the news chip retires on a clock and this stylesheet collapsed its box, dropping the hero about a hundred pixels into the mark. Measured identical on main and on this branch before the fix. And the Manrope subset carried neither character in the name Jelena Tesic, who leads the team this deck is about, so the font range now covers Latin Extended-A at a measured cost of 14,932 bytes across three faces.
  • EIGHTEEN HOUSE STYLE VIOLATIONS WERE THIS RUN'S OWN WRITING. Ten sentences over the thirty word backstop, in two item summaries, three verification notes, one public access field and three claim texts the article page renders. main was clean, so every one of them was written today. All split at a clause.
  • THE AUDIT TRAIL HAD ITS TWO SOURCE CLASSES SWAPPED. aggregates.json declared the university release and the two TxDOT pages as the three first party accounts and the two journal papers as the official records, which is the exact inverse of claims.json's own source_type and of sources_block.py's name table. The published sentence was never wrong because the script computes it. aggregate_check could not see it because both partitions are three documents and two.
  • A ROBOTS DISALLOW WAS WALKED INTO by this run's own re-verification probe, which fetched capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs before a FORBIDDEN list was added to it. Recorded in the field log rather than quietly fixed. The registry's list lives in a file a scratch fetcher never reads, and scripts/shared/ has no shared fetch helper, which is the real gap.
  • Two record items are held for a maintainer: an inconsistent statewide treatment between tx-2026-0135 and tx-2026-0143, and a district the gazetteer cannot place because this repository holds no city to county crosswalk.
  • The scanner ceiling was not read. No Supabase connector is attached to this session.
  • WHAT THE PANEL FOUND AND THIS RUN DID NOT FIX, so the next one has it. The craft judge scored artwork 6.0 and named frame 7, the deck's turn, as its weakest drawing: the office chair its own technique line names is absent, and the figure's forearm does not visibly join the hand on the desk. Two judges also read the value arc as collapsed, with seven of nine frames at median L* 6.1 against a storyboard that plans a dark frame and a light one. Neither is a hard fail and both are craft rather than fact, so they are in the backlog rather than in another repair round.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Texas State University's AI pavement inspection method, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Who decides whether a crack counts?

A rater used to measure distress by hand on a sampled portion of the pavement section. That put a person in the traffic and the weather. Texas State University now reads that damage at pixel level from paired photos and depth maps. TxDOT funds the work and donated the van.

A score of 70 or above counts as good or better. Tracking that quality is how the agency finds roads needing repair. The team's own 2025 paper says a pavement engineer still has to verify what the machine returns.

Nine frames run from a rater on the fog line to the empty farm road the money is aimed at.

The release puts the project in a second phase and stops at closer to statewide deployment. It names three next steps and dates none. What would have to change before the score on a road you drive moves?

#TxDOT #TexasStateUniversity #PavementConditionScore

The machine changed itself

  • docket_calendar.py labels the award expiry kind and derives its far-date test from the horizon's own rule
    An item admitted this run carries a key date in August 2029. The kind had no English label and would have reached a reader as the slug `expires`, and the emptiness test asked for a calendar at a hardcoded 2031-01-01 whose two year window now contains that date. Two self-test failures on correct data, on the same file that carries a note about this exact mistake from two weeks earlier.
  • The article page stopped printing two full stops on a line ending in a quoted sentence
    The terminator test read the last character only. Three frames this run set a quoted fragment and the story section doubled the period on the one whose full stop is inside the quote.
  • Five proposals written to knowledge/carousel/UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md and NOT made
    Each is upgrade lane or out of a routine's reach: caption_check refusing the word mine, build_copy deriving the hook from the largest laid out node, a gradient under a coarse halftone banding into what qa.py reads as a rule through type, a screened field on a dark register not registering as a silhouette, and an axis bound being the one disposition aggregate_check and numeral_trace cannot express between them.

Each reverts on its own commit.

Notes

THE RECORD IS DONE AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS MOST. 99 items came due, all 99 were re-verified, 130 items stand on the record and the backlog is zero at wake and zero at ship. One item genuinely moved and was corrected. Three were admitted, each citing a primary source. THE DECK IS FINISHED AND SCORED. Round 3 of the panel read 6.920 against a 6.8 bar with no hard fail from any of the three judges. It took three rounds to get there and the middle one is why. Round 1 read 6.786, under the bar with no hard fail, and every finding the three judges converged on was repaired. The largest was that the deck's one TURN was marking an empty desk. Frame 7's hand sprite had been standing on the floor 250 px below the granite sheet, because a sprite stands on the ground plane and the hand's parts were declared from zero. Three readers found the symptom and none could see the cause. Round 2 lost all three judges to the same session quota inside a second of each other. A single retry, taken when the quota returned, raised the run's only HARD FAIL and it was right. Frame 8 printed 1.0 and 0 as its axis bounds, and neither figure comes from the record. Both numeral gates were green over it, which is the part worth keeping: aggregate_check cannot declare a bare axis label, and numeral_trace passed the digits by the coincidence its own docstring says it cannot see. The frame now draws both rules and NAMES them, and prints no bound figure. WHAT ELSE THE RUN FOUND IN ITS OWN WORK, none of it from a judge. Two claims on the record asserted more than their quote proved, one of them a city that was load bearing for a county assignment, and both sources do say it so both quotes were repaired rather than the claims softened. The article page was titled after its own directory. An unscored run could publish at all. Eighteen house style violations, every one written today. And the audit trail had its two source classes exactly swapped. WHY IT DID NOT MERGE, AND IT IS NOT THE DECK. CI went green on the head before last, on all seven jobs. Then main moved twice and the second one conflicted, because another pull request fixed the same front page collision from the other side. Both fixes are kept and the merge is resolved and pushed. No workflow fired on that merge commit, the pull request reports zero checks, and dispatching one returns 403 Resource not accessible by integration. A green run on an earlier head says nothing about this one, and the two ways to force a run are both forbidden here. WHAT TO DO WITH THIS. Nothing is required and nothing is broken. The deck is scored, every gate is green, and the only missing thing is a CI run on one commit that this session cannot cause. A maintainer looking at pull request 298 will either see checks that arrived late and can merge it, or can merge it on the strength of the seven green jobs on the commit before the merge. The images in this email point at the run BRANCH rather than main, because nothing merged yet.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck did NOT merge, so nothing here is on main and there is nothing to post. The links resolve against the run branch for as long as it exists.
